question.text: Under Section 194LBB of the ITA, when an Investment Fund (Cat I/II AIF) distributes non-business income to a RESIDENT unit-holder, at what rate is TDS deducted?

answer.text: At the rate of the highest slab applicable to the unit-holder

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 194LBB(a) mandates TDS at 10% on all non-business income distributed or credited by an Investment Fund to a resident investor. This is a flat rate irrespective of head of income. The unit-holder claims this TDS as credit in their return. **The Trap:** Option A is 194LBC for securitisation trusts. Option C is the non-resident dividend rate under 194LBB(b). Option D confuses TDS with final tax. **Cross-Exam Context:** III-A/C Compliance tests this TDS literal; XIX-C tests how it integrates with distribution waterfall calculations. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** For distributions NEAR year-end, remember Section 115UB's 'deemed credit' rule: if income is not actually paid out, it is deemed credited to the unit-holder on 31 March. Trigger 194LBB on the deemed-credit date — not on the actual payment date.
